title: Review of c02's FCH chemoton: on fresh seeds 5-7 a K-bearing vesicle forms in 1 of 3 runs (seed 7); a per-vesicle local feed cut shrinks the target to 0.58-0.67x while its fed twin holds, but nobody dies and other bodies lose 5-32% through the shared bath
summary: I ran labkit packs of the unchanged world on new seeds 5 and 7, plus seed 6 inside a fork test. From noise every seed makes FCH bilayers, rods and rings. A vesicle with catalyst beaded along its bilayer forms only on seed 7 (a figure-8 double vesicle). On seeds 5 and 6 the catalyst sits in a filled rod, and the K-free rings persist on amphiphile from the bath. For the disputed E, I used L4c's local-ablation route (localcut.py): at t=300 the precursor feed is cut only in a disc around the largest K-bearing body, alongside an exact fed twin, and run to t=600. On c02's seed 0 (the claimed multilamellar vesicle) and on seed 7 (the figure-8), the target's amphiphile goes to 0.58x and 0.67x (twins 1.04x and 1.12x) and its K to 0.29x and 0.39x. It shrinks to a smaller double ring but does not die within 300 t. The other K-bearing bodies drop to 0.95x and 0.68x (twins 1.07x and 0.93x), and K-free bodies also fall, because all bodies draw on one bath pool of amphiphile.

verdicts.limitation: E: amphiphile is made only by K from P and decays at kap, so dependence holds by construction (scored under mechanism). No individual died within 300 t of either cut; they shrink, and the shrink rate is falling by t=600. Bodies are not metabolically separate: the product leaks into a shared bath pool, so cutting one body's feed also costs other bodies 5-32% beyond their twins, and K-free rings live on that pool. B: the K-on-bilayer individual of the claim formed in 1/3 of my fresh seeds, and when the catalyst forms it is more often a filled rod. The K layer is placed by a mobility gate written against u, but K is made in place by its own autocatalysis, not by the medium, so I count it under the quasi-equilibrium clause. No matched Laplacian-only control, and no dt or grid test.
